samples.summary: New REST insert/delete/move endpoints bypass the pivot-sheet structural guard the editor enforces
samples.evidence: The editor path refuses structural edits on a pivot output sheet: `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1236` (`insertRows`), `:1244` (`deleteRows`), `:1252`/`:1260` (columns) all `if (this.pivotDefinition) return;`. The new endpoints only check the *document* type (`assertSheetDocument`, worksheet-structure.controller.ts:56) and never look at `tabs[tabId].kind === 'pivot'` or `ws.pivotTable`, so `POST .../tabs/:tabId/insert|delete|move` will splice rows/columns straight into a pivot-generated worksheet — a state the engine assumes cannot occur and which the next pivot recalculation will fight with. The fix belongs on the new controller (add a pivot check alongside `assertSheetDocument`).

samples.summary: Backend calls applyWorksheetShift alone, but the engine's only other caller complements it with filter/hidden/freeze remapping that the API path now skips
samples.evidence: `Sheet.shiftCells` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1287) calls `store.shiftCells(...)` — the YorkieStore wrapper around `applyWorksheetShift` — and then does the rest of the operation itself: `shiftFilterState` (sheet.ts:1317), `shiftUserHiddenState` (sheet.ts:1318), freeze-pane adjustment + `store.setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:1334-1357), and `recalculateAllFormulaCells()` (sheet.ts:1361). `applyWorksheetShift` in packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts touches none of `ws.filter`, `ws.hiddenRows`, `ws.hiddenColumns`, `ws.frozenRows`, `ws.frozenCols`. The new controller calls the helper alone, so a row inserted through the API leaves the persisted filter range, hidden-row indices and freeze boundary pointing at the pre-shift positions — visible corruption the moment a client opens the document. Same for `applyWorksheetMove` (`Sheet.moveCells`, sheet.ts:1453-1473, plus `moveUserHiddenState` sheet.ts:1759).

samples.summary: Structural edits through the API leave cached formula results (`v`) stale, unlike every editor-side caller
samples.evidence: `applyWorksheetShift` rewrites formula text (`shiftFormula`) but not the cached value; the editor always follows with `recalculateAllFormulaCells()` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1361). Nothing in packages/backend/src recalculates (grep for calculate/recalc in backend returns only comments), so `=A2` rewritten to `=A3` keeps the old cached `v` until a browser opens the doc. Pre-existing for the cells API, but structural edits shift entire regions at once, widening it.

samples.summary: Design doc still points at the moved frontend module paths (nested docs are not link-checked by CI)
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/comments.md:75 lists `yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts` in the frontend spreadsheet module tree and :289 says `// packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts` for `deleteThreadsForAxis`; the file now lives at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts. The top-level docs path check does not recurse into docs/design/<topic>/, so nothing catches this.

samples.summary: insertWorksheetAxis/deleteWorksheetAxis/moveWorksheetAxis are newly re-exported from the package root but have no consumer outside worksheet-structure.ts
samples.evidence: Grep across the repo finds references only inside packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:357 and the index re-export itself; knip's unused-exports lane is likely to flag them.

finding.summary: New REST insert/delete/move endpoints bypass the pivot-sheet structural guard the editor enforces
finding.evidence: The editor path refuses structural edits on a pivot output sheet: `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1236` (`insertRows`), `:1244` (`deleteRows`), `:1252`/`:1260` (columns) all `if (this.pivotDefinition) return;`. The new endpoints only check the *document* type (`assertSheetDocument`, worksheet-structure.controller.ts:56) and never look at `tabs[tabId].kind === 'pivot'` or `ws.pivotTable`, so `POST .../tabs/:tabId/insert|delete|move` will splice rows/columns straight into a pivot-generated worksheet — a state the engine assumes cannot occur and which the next pivot recalculation will fight with. The fix belongs on the new controller (add a pivot check alongside `assertSheetDocument`).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The pivot structural guard exists exactly as claimed: sheet.ts:1236/1244/1252/1260 each early-return `if (this.pivotDefinition) return;` for insertRows/deleteRows/insertColumns/deleteColumns (part of a broader set of pivot guards at :1085, :1159, :2166, :4150, :4368). The new controller's only precondition is `assertSheetDocument` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:51-62), which compares the *document* type (`doc.type !== 'sheet'`) and never inspects `root.sheets[tabId].pivotTable` or `root.tabs[tabId].kind`; `worksheetOrThrow` (:64-71) only checks existence. insertAxis (:111), deleteAxis (:127) and moveAxis (:140) therefore reach applyShift/applyWorksheetMove with no pivot check. Downstream is also unguarded: applyWorksheetShift (worksheet-structure.ts:273-288) and applyWorksheetMove (:347-357) splice axes unconditionally; the only pivot-aware code there (:441, :471) repoints a pivot's sourceRange when the SOURCE tab shifts and does not refuse a shift of the pivot output tab. The pivot marker is available on the exact data the controller holds (worksheet-document.ts:99 `pivotTable`, :119/:125 `kind: SheetKind`). So a REST caller can splice rows/columns into a pivot-generated worksheet, violating an invariant the sheets model enforces — a new entry point bypassing an existing guard, squarely in the blast-radius lane at major severity. I could not establish any refutation ground: the code is present as described, no auth/scope guard on the route (:44) covers this, and the fact that sibling controllers (e.g. worksheet.controller.ts:169 PUT merges vs. the mergeSelection pivot guard at sheet.ts:4150) share the omission does not make this instance unreal or unreachable.

finding.evidence: `Sheet.shiftCells` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1287) calls `store.shiftCells(...)` — the YorkieStore wrapper around `applyWorksheetShift` — and then does the rest of the operation itself: `shiftFilterState` (sheet.ts:1317), `shiftUserHiddenState` (sheet.ts:1318), freeze-pane adjustment + `store.setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:1334-1357), and `recalculateAllFormulaCells()` (sheet.ts:1361). `applyWorksheetShift` in packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts touches none of `ws.filter`, `ws.hiddenRows`, `ws.hiddenColumns`, `ws.frozenRows`, `ws.frozenCols`. The new controller calls the helper alone, so a row inserted through the API leaves the persisted filter range, hidden-row indices and freeze boundary pointing at the pre-shift positions — visible corruption the moment a client opens the document. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. applyWorksheetShift (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:273-345) and applyWorksheetMove (347-418) remap rowOrder/colOrder, formulas, dimensions, styles, rangeStyles, conditional formats, validations, merges and anchors, but never touch ws.filter, ws.hiddenRows, ws.hiddenColumns, ws.frozenRows or ws.frozenCols. The engine's only other caller does that work itself: Sheet.shiftCells calls store.shiftCells (sheet.ts:1287 -> yorkie-store.ts:453-477, the applyWorksheetShift wrapper) and then shiftFilterState (sheet.ts:1317), shiftUserHiddenState (sheet.ts:1318), the freeze-pane adjust + store.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:1334-1357), recalculateAllFormulaCells (sheet.ts:1361) and recomputeFilterHiddenRows (sheet.ts:1363); the move path mirrors it at sheet.ts:1506-1507. These are persisted, index-based document fields (worksheet-document.ts:47-98) that the client rehydrates via store.getFilterState()/getHiddenState() (sheet.ts:541,566 -> yorkie-store.ts:987-1113) and that the backend itself exposes (worksheet.controller.ts:70,114-137). The new controller calls the helper alone (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:186-199 for insert/delete, 147-162 for move) with no filter/hidden/freeze remapping anywhere in it or in packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts. So a row inserted/deleted/moved through the reachable POST insert/delete/move endpoints leaves the persisted filter range, hidden indices and freeze boundary pointing at pre-shift positions - an invariant another module relies on, violated where that module reads it. No guard makes it unreachable; in lane (partial reuse of an engine contract whose other caller supplies the missing half) and blocking at major.
